items.detail: **Wednesday's July CPI** (8:30am ET) is the week's dominant event, with forecasts near **3.4% headline and roughly 2.5% core year-over-year** after June's 3.5% headline, and **July PPI follows Thursday**.
items.why: Friday's payrolls miss flipped September pricing from a hike to a hold, so a hot CPI or PPI would put the hike case back on the table and hit the rate-sensitive megacaps that drove the index to its 7,746 record, while another cool print would validate the melt-up.

items.detail: Q2 earnings thin out but the AI-capex tape gets two checks: **Cisco reports Q4 FY26 after Wednesday's close** and **Applied Materials reports Thursday after the close**.
items.why: AMD's nearly 9% after-hours drop on soft guidance despite record revenue showed how much AI upside is already priced in, so networking and semi-equipment order commentary is the cleanest test of whether the capex story broadens or narrows further.

items.detail: **Friday brings July retail sales**, expected up about **0.2%** in line with June, alongside the preliminary August University of Michigan sentiment reading.
items.why: With payrolls now shrinking, retail sales is the market's next read on whether the consumer is cracking too — a soft print would deepen the growth scare that a Fed-hold rally cannot indefinitely paper over.

items.detail: **India's July CPI lands Wednesday**, with June's print at **4.38%** and ICRA looking for a hardening toward roughly **4.6%** as the Middle East energy shock feeds through to transport and food prices.
items.why: An upside surprise would strengthen the minority case that the RBI's next move is a hike rather than a hold, pressuring the private banks that already led Friday's selloff and threatening the 24,400 support the index needs to hold.

items.detail: **Friday, August 14 is the SEBI deadline** for June-quarter results, with thousands of companies still to report and **Grasim Industries reporting Wednesday**; **July WPI also releases Friday** after June's 9.87%.
items.why: A deadline-week flood of Q1 FY27 numbers concentrates single-stock risk into a few sessions, and with Nifty 50 earnings so far showing healthy revenue but softer profit growth, the aggregate margin picture decides whether the two-week rally has fundamental backing.

items.detail: Foreign flows go in as the structural bid, with **FIIs net buyers of about ₹2,887 crore in the cash market so far in August**, while crude's rebound to roughly $83 and US–Iran talks remain the swing factor.
items.why: The FII bid is the mechanism holding the index above 24,400, and it is a derivative of global risk appetite and cheap oil — a hot US CPI or a crude spike on Hormuz headlines would reverse both at once and stall the push toward the 24,774 breakout level.

items.detail: With Bitcoin entering near **$65,144** and Ether still capped below **$2,000**, **Wednesday's US CPI is the week's only first-tier catalyst** — there is no crypto-specific scheduled event to compete with it now that the Senate is in recess until September 11.
items.why: Crypto only joined last week's rally once the payrolls miss shifted the Fed toward a hold, so it is trading as a pure duration asset — a hot CPI hits it harder than equities, and a cool one is the most likely route to Ether reclaiming $2,000.

items.detail: **Monday delivers a cliff unlock of roughly $471.6 million in RAIN**, about **3.23% of supply** and the single largest token unlock of August, landing at the end of a concentrated three-day stretch that also included STABLE and ADI.
items.why: Cliff unlocks add immediate float that has to be absorbed, so an outsized drop would signal thin altcoin bids beneath the majors, while a contained response would suggest real demand has returned rather than just ETF-driven Bitcoin buying.

items.detail: Watch the daily spot ETF flow prints for a **fourth consecutive week of net inflows** after last week's **$750 million-plus**, against 2026 flows still net negative at about **$5.2 billion** and Ether products bleeding while Bitcoin gathers.
items.why: Institutional buying, not retail, has been the marginal price support through this recovery, so a flow reversal on a hot CPI would remove the bid that has underwritten the move off the lows — and the Bitcoin-in, Ether-out split shows the rebound is far narrower than the headline number suggests.

crossCuttingTheme: Wednesday, August 12 is the hinge for all three markets: US July CPI at 8:30am ET will either confirm or reverse the shift from a September hike to a hold that powered last week's records, and India's own July CPI prints the same day — a hot US number simultaneously threatens the rate-sensitive megacaps at 7,746, the foreign bid holding the Nifty above 24,400, and crypto's rate-driven bounce off the lows.
